title: Proxy Voting Record
description: Deterministic proxy-voting record arithmetic over caller-declared synthetic inputs. From a declared meeting record date and vote deadline, declared record-date positions, and a declared voting instruction, computes entitled_shares as the sum of record-date position shares, days_before_deadline as whole UTC calendar days from the declared received date to the declared deadline, instruction_within_deadline, and an overall verdict of VOTE_RECORDED or INSTRUCTION_LATE with the late instruction still reported. No registrar, no share register, no SSR tape, no borrow list, no cutoff feed, no network, no clock.

positions.description: Declared record-date positions; entitlement is the sum of their shares.

received.description: Date the voting instruction was received, YYYY-MM-DD.

entitled_shares.description: Sum of record-date position shares; null on the fail-closed path.

instruction_within_deadline.description: True when the instruction received date is not after the vote deadline.

days_before_deadline.description: Whole UTC calendar days from received to the deadline; negative when late.

trace.description: Full arithmetic trace, or the fail-closed reasons naming each rejected input.

mcp_tool_definition.name: compute_proxy_voting_record
mcp_tool_definition.description: Computes a proxy voting record from declared meeting dates, record-date positions, and a voting instruction: entitled shares as the position sum, whole days before the declared vote deadline, deadline status, and an overall VOTE_RECORDED or INSTRUCTION_LATE verdict. Record arithmetic over caller-declared synthetic inputs only: no registrar check, no share register, no voting advice, and no instruction is transmitted anywhere.

instruction.description: received (YYYY-MM-DD) and direction (for, against, abstain, withhold)

source: authored by PROXY-VOTING-BUILD-1 per PROXY-VOTING-BUILD-SPEC.md. Scope positioning: a record-keeping calculator over caller-declared synthetic inputs, not voting advice, not a solicitation, and not a submission channel; absent or invalid inputs are refused fail-closed and named, never silently repaired.
